items.capacityTheme: Unlock analyst and operator bandwidth through one flagship decision layer
items.boardQuestion: Where can one system absorb more decision demand without adding more managerial overhead?
items.currentPosture: The AI flagship is reducing wrapper noise and centralizing memo work, but leadership still needs one cleaner proof packet on absorbed decision load.
items.requiredProof: Lower coordination overhead, faster memo turnarounds, and wider reuse by operating teams.
items.headline: AI can absorb more decision demand without adding another layer of workflow sprawl.
items.narrative: The strongest signal is that one system is already carrying more cross-functional decision work with less orchestration drag.
items.nextMove: Package absorbed decision load and faster memo cycles into one board-safe capacity packet.

items.capacityTheme: Stabilize admin bandwidth before another identity consolidation ask
items.boardQuestion: Which lane has strategic importance but still cannot absorb more change without burning scarce operators?
items.currentPosture: Identity controls are clearer than before, but remediation ownership still runs thin and admin bandwidth remains brittle.
items.requiredProof: Cleaner handoffs, lower exception churn, and stronger admin coverage across identity controls.
items.headline: Identity should stabilize operator bandwidth before leadership adds more consolidation pressure.
items.narrative: The board story here is not rapid expansion; it is to prove that control owners can absorb more load without reopening drift.
items.nextMove: Stabilize admin bandwidth and prove lower exception churn before new consolidation motions land.

items.capacityTheme: Hold expansion until reporting teams stop spending cycles on explanation loops
items.boardQuestion: Where does capacity look available on paper but still get consumed by reporting friction?
items.currentPosture: Revenue systems reduced some backlog noise, but reporting operators still burn cycles reconciling overlapping answer paths.
items.requiredProof: Fewer manual explanation loops, cleaner reporting ownership, and sustained reduction in reporting churn.
items.headline: Revenue has latent capacity, but it should not be expanded until reporting friction drops further.
items.narrative: The strongest board signal here is cleaner throughput, not another claim about general revenue-system leverage.
items.nextMove: Hold wider expansion until reporting teams spend more hours on decisions and fewer on reconciliation.

items.capacityTheme: Escalate fragmented teams before promising more throughput
items.boardQuestion: Which lane still has too many disconnected queues and not enough shared operator bandwidth to scale safely?
items.currentPosture: Payments, treasury, merchant review, and KYC all exist, but the capacity story is fragmented and still depends on too many isolated proofs.
items.requiredProof: Shared ownership, lower queue handoff cost, and stronger sequencing confidence across the FinTech family.
items.headline: FinTech should be escalated before the board treats it as a lane with expandable capacity.
items.narrative: The right move is to expose the fragmentation now rather than overstate how much throughput this stack can absorb.
items.nextMove: Escalate fragmented queues and thin bandwidth into one diligence packet before another growth ask reaches the board.

items.capacityTheme: Unlock buyer-path bandwidth through one reusable trust-answer core
items.boardQuestion: Where can one answer system absorb more buyer load without creating more support overhead?
items.currentPosture: Trust evidence is reusable, procurement packaging is consolidated, and the answer core is ready to absorb more buyer volume.
items.requiredProof: Shorter cycle times, fewer custom packets, and wider answer reuse across procurement and trust flows.
items.headline: Procurement can absorb more buyer demand through one reusable answer core.
items.narrative: The board signal is not just fewer packets; it is a buyer path that scales without eating more internal attention.
items.nextMove: Show reusable trust answers and lower cycle times in one board-readable capacity packet.

items.capacityTheme: Stabilize regulated team capacity before another throughput promise
items.boardQuestion: Which regulated lane has real progress but still needs tighter throughput continuity before expansion?
items.currentPosture: The biotech stack is credible, but leadership still needs clearer proof that teams can absorb more volume without weakening controls.
items.requiredProof: Sustained case flow, stable control quality, and no new review bottlenecks across GxP, CAPA, specimen, and safety lanes.
items.headline: Biotech is a stabilize-first lane: stronger regulated team capacity now, wider expansion later.
items.narrative: The board story is that regulated teams can carry more load without eroding continuity or control quality.
items.nextMove: Stabilize throughput evidence and publish a continuity packet before wider expansion claims are made.
